waveOwnership: new docs/specs/tests only; no runtime visual mutation

decisions.statement: Mazer's target product is the Fawxzzy Precision Arcade direction: a mobile-first, installable, precision-arcade maze game where the board is the hero and application chrome only explains, enables, or protects play.

Phaser owns world/maze simulation-facing presentation (board rendering, title path animation, world-space entities, camera/world effects, menu demonstration maze, world diagnostics). DOM owns application shell, forms, HUD, touch controls, settings, dialogs, guide/confirmations, and system chrome. Semantic tokens, state registry, commands, view models, responsive metrics, platform profiles, topology/path geometry, icon definitions, motion semantics, diagnostics schema, and capture IDs are shared contracts owned by neither renderer alone.

The shipping maze presentation remains connected corridors, not exposed square tiles. Tile topology stays canonical underlying data; visible square-tile boundaries are optional proof/debug treatment only, never the shipping default.
Mobile, desktop, TV, OBS, arcade, and cyberdeck are output profiles, not public themes. Profiles vary layout and density; they never vary brand identity.

One canonical player-facing theme (Fawxzzy Precision Arcade) replaces the public theme matrix. The noir, ember, vellum, aurora, and monolith theme variants are archived historical experiments, not live public options, and no public theme switch ships in the canonical product.
proof-surfaces.html and visual-proof.html remain internal verification tools (projection QA / critical internal verification), not public product, and are not release-gating core surfaces.

Watch Pass (watch-pass-setup.html, watch-pass-preview.html) remains an incubating companion product behind a feature boundary. watch-pass-paywall.html is a commerce prototype only; no production billing or entitlement claim is permitted until real billing exists.
planet3d.html is an isolated lab, explicitly excluded from core-v1 release acceptance.
future-phaser.html is slated for adapter-lesson extraction (its useful adapter contracts become tests) and then entrypoint retirement.

MenuScene.ts is decomposed through characterization and adapters across later waves, not replaced in one rewrite. A big-bang rewrite is rejected because core scene ownership is migration-sensitive and mechanics are already proof-backed.

The former PR #83 and PR #131 implementation vehicles are superseded. Shared UI and authentication paths are no longer held behind a branch-specific exception; each path may change only in its currently active integrator wave, resolved from an explicit per-wave dependency graph (not one total ordering), with a fresh current-main preflight and exclusive active-writer ownership. A wave's own historical (completed) ownership of a path never grants it permission to keep changing that path after an explicit handoff to a new active owner; two waves with no dependency relationship to each other (e.g. an auth-domain wave and a renderer wave that both merely depend on the same prior wave) may hold active ownership of different paths at once without a dependency edge being invented between them.

Wave 2A introduces only stateless, renderer-neutral DOM construction primitives. These modules own native semantics, accessibility, and primitive styling but do not import MenuScene, authentication, stores, commands, network clients, persistence, or runtime state; they remain unmounted until a later assigned integrator wave.

Wave 2A.1 extends the unmounted DOM foundation with controlled settings rows, sections, switches, radio segments, native scroll ownership, nonblocking status, and safe-default confirmation primitives. Persistence, commands, runtime mounting, provider access, and product appearance remain owned by later integrator waves.

No source lane may claim the redesign complete until the final acceptance matrix (the nine-point Definition of Complete) passes and old duplicated UI paths are removed or formally retained with an owner and purpose.

phaserOwns: world-space player, start, goal, trail, cues, and future Fragment entities

integratorWaveOwnership.modeNote: Each assignment declares its own dependsOn (an array of prerequisite wave ids), not a position in one shared total order -- a wave with no dependency relationship to another may be active at the same time, over different paths, without a dependency edge between them. status distinguishes completed (historical record; no longer enforceable as active ownership of its paths) from active (the current, single, exclusive writer for its paths). Exactly one assignment may be status:'active' for any given path at a time; multiple completed assignments may reference the same path as history (a real handoff), which is not a violation.

assignments.completionNote: PR #343, squash-merged to main. Made the Wave 1A shared UI command/state contracts load-bearing against the real running scene. src/scenes/MenuScene.ts's active ownership hands off to Wave 4D-A below (Navigation Core runtime); src/state/uiLegacyBridge.ts has no active claimant after this handoff and is available to a future wave that needs it.

assignments.note: Implements the frozen docs/assets/reference/navigation-core-v1/ visual authority into the real Phaser runtime. Depends only on Wave 3A's completion (the command bridge it builds on top of); no dependency edge to Wave 3B is required or implied -- the two waves own disjoint paths and neither's work gates the other. src/render/navigationCoreTrail.ts is a new pure geometry/color/shine module extracted out of MenuScene.ts for the continuous trail (arc-length path building, corner rounding, energy-palette color sampling, shared shine timing) -- added here explicitly rather than left unowned. src/render/navigationCoreTrailCanvas.ts is a second new module claimed here: a real 2D-canvas compositor for the same trail (continuous multi-point stroke chunks with real line joins, plus a genuine shadowBlur-based glow), replacing Graphics vector strokes once those proved unable to avoid a corner self-intersection artifact -- this game runs Phaser.CANVAS, so Phaser's WebGL-only postFX/preFX blur was never an available alternative. src/render/navigationCorePlayerGlowCanvas.ts is a third new module: the same real-shadowBlur-compositor technique applied to the play-mode player marker's two drop-shadow glow layers, replacing two flat hard-edged fillRoundedRect 'shells' that read as nested solid bodies rather than light. src/render/navigationCoreGoalHaloCanvas.ts is a fourth new module: a real canvas radial-gradient halo for the goal star, replacing two flat fillCircle discs that read as sharply bounded target rings; scoped to only the real on-board goal marker, not the separate Options/Guide legend icon. src/scenes/BootScene.ts is also claimed here: it gained a load-bearing derived-texture generator (the floor-tile interior crop the corridor material depends on) as part of this same visual authority, with a failure-safe fallback that disables the floor-texture accent rather than ever showing Phaser's missing-texture placeholder or the raw bordered source. Navigation Core v1 implementation completed and squash-merged to main in PR #345 at commit daf92fd4cf404c9471b55030416d366af201399f. src/scenes/MenuScene.ts, previously also claimed here, was handed off to Wave 4D-B below once that wave's runtime-integration slice genuinely needed to touch it (a real QA-visible teleport-anchor pose preview) -- this assignment's own remaining paths (BootScene.ts and the navigationCore*.ts modules) still have no other claimant, so it stays 'active' rather than 'completed' for those, matching REQUIRED_INTEGRATOR_WAVE_BY_PATH's continued pin of BootScene.ts here.

Implements Teleport System v1 (docs/assets/reference/teleport-system-v1/) runtime integration. src/render/teleportPrimaryAnchor.ts (PR #346, squash-merged to main at commit bf4e4bec92392efa9ad1e6cef9216befc634385b) is the pure primary-anchor selection policy: nearest eligible anchor by inward beam-port distance, fixed anchor-ID tie-break, persisted across outbound/stored/delivering, remapped only when the held anchor becomes ineligible or disappears. src/render/teleportAnchorPose.ts is a second pure module added in this slice: resolves real anchor poses (position, target-facing rotation, transformed measured beam-port) and clearance (a conservative bounding-box footprint against real HUD/safe-area exclusion rectangles) from real viewport/target/shell-size inputs, reproducing MenuScene.ts's own existing perimeter-anchor position formula (cross-checked in tests against the real resolveLegacyMenuPathTitleOrbitPose export) while using the frozen contract's own precisely MEASURED shell-tip angle (-59.43 degrees, from the derivative manifest's alpha-channel bounding analysis) rather than MenuScene's own admittedly-approximate -45-degree constant used for its unrelated ambient title-orbit sigils. src/scenes/MenuScene.ts is claimed here as of this slice, handed off from Wave 4D-A (see that assignment's note) -- this slice adds a real, opt-in QA pose-preview surface that computes real candidate poses/eligibility from the live scene and repositions one of the scene's existing orbit-diamond image pool slots to the selector's chosen pose, restoring it afterward; it does not touch Wave 4D-A's remaining paths (BootScene.ts, the navigationCore*.ts modules) and does not replace or rewrite the existing spawn-beam/player-transfer choreography (src/legacy-runtime/legacyPlayerTransfer.ts remains the relevant timing infrastructure, unchanged and un-owned by this wave). Depends on 4D-A's completion because both share Navigation Core's energy-palette contract, not because this slice touches any of 4D-A's remaining paths. The full conduit/spawn/extraction choreography replacing the current player-transfer beams is explicitly deferred to a later slice, not claimed here. src/render/teleportTransferPresentation.ts is a third pure module, added in the next slice (branch claude/mazer-wave4d-b-transfer-renderer, opened after PR #347 merged to main at commit d40b41f66e53b76a9dd04eb8903dec01d470c633): a stateless presentation projection for a single-primary gameplay transfer conduit, layered directly on the existing single authoritative lifecycle (src/legacy-runtime/legacyPlayerTransfer.ts, unchanged, not owned by this wave) rather than a second gameplay state machine -- it derives conduit open/closed fraction, packet position/visibility, and source/target flare intensity for both extraction (packet travels from the real goal toward the held primary's measured port) and delivery (packet travels from the primary toward the real next-start tile) directions, always taking the currently-held primary's pose as a plain input; it does not select or remap an anchor itself, and is not yet wired into any renderer or scene call site. The actual conduit/packet pixel renderer, real scene integration replacing the ambient eight-origin volley for gameplay transfers, and real goal-to-delivery evidence remain explicitly deferred to subsequent commits in this same wave, not claimed complete here. Two checkpoint fixes then corrected real presentation-contract gaps (still on the same branch, prior to any renderer existing): the required-tests registry omission for teleportTransferPresentation.test.ts was fixed, and the extraction direction gained a real closure envelope (a short taper after the resolver's own outbound-to-stored boundary, rather than a hard cut) plus a genuine reduced-motion crossfade (previously unreachable, since the underlying resolver skips the 'outbound' phase entirely under reduced motion) -- both derived from the existing raw elapsed-ms inputs, with no new gameplay clock. src/render/teleportTransferConduitCanvas.ts is a fourth pure-ish module (a Canvas-2D compositor, not state logic): consumes teleportTransferPresentation.ts's output to draw the conduit stroke (glow pass plus crisp core pass, reusing navigationCoreTrailCanvas.ts's own round-join/shadowBlur technique), the traveling packet, and the target flare (reusing navigationCoreGoalHaloCanvas.ts's drawGoalHaloToCanvasContext directly, unmodified). Draws zero pixels whenever openFraction <= 0 (asserted in tests via a fake-context call-count of exactly 0), reuses one shared caller-supplied energyColor (from the existing resolveLegacyIridescentMidnightColor palette, the same one the play trail already carries) across the conduit/packet/flare so all three always read as one continuous material rather than independently-colored parts, and documents that masking the conduit's near-source pixels behind the real shell Image is a caller draw-order responsibility, not something it clips internally. Still not yet wired into any scene call site. Real scene integration (replacing the ambient eight-origin volley for gameplay transfers specifically, while leaving it in place for menu/title choreography), a real held-transfer session tied to actual goal-acceptance, and real goal-to-delivery gameplay evidence remain the explicitly deferred next commits in this same wave. The full single-primary gameplay conduit was completed across several further correction rounds (owner-authorized calmer trail/conduit palette included) and squash-merged to main in PR #348 at commit b0b99a9ca53acf36586881ef3fce3feef2994c4e. src/scenes/MenuScene.ts, previously also claimed here, was handed off to Wave 4E below once that wave's own slice needed to touch it (the background starfield twinkle, unrelated to Teleport) -- this assignment's own remaining paths (the four teleport*.ts modules) still have no other claimant, so it stays 'active' rather than 'completed' for those, matching Wave 4D-A's own identical MenuScene.ts handoff precedent above.

World Identity: the menu/backdrop starfield and related ambient world presentation, starting with a bounded correctness slice for the background star twinkle (owner-reported: stars 'switch colors like a strobe' instead of smoothly brightening/dimming and growing/shrinking). Confirmed real defect, not a tuning issue: MenuScene.ts's per-frame star-draw loop derived its own 'seed' fresh every frame from the star's own (continuously drifting) position -- `((star.x * 9973) + (star.y * 6151)) % 1` -- which looks like a stable position-keyed hash but isn't: multiplying a smoothly-changing float by a large constant before taking it mod 1 amplifies even sub-pixel motion into an effectively unrelated result every frame. Measured live: a star moving at its own ordinary drift speed produced an uncorrelated new value in [0, 1) on almost every real frame (a 30-sample real-time trace jumped the full range with no pattern). Every visual that value fed -- the sparkle hue for the brightest ~5% of stars, the round-star white/blue/warm color bucket, and each star's own twinkle PERIOD -- was silently re-randomizing every frame instead of the single fixed-per-star identity the surrounding code's own comments already describe wanting ('each star gets its own period... so they don't all pulse in lockstep'). Fixed by adding a real persisted `seed` field to `LegacyMenuBackdropStar` (src/legacy-runtime/legacyMenuBackdrop.ts), assigned once at creation and reassigned only at genuine rebirth (resetLegacyMenuBackdropStarNearWarpOrigin) -- never mid-life -- and reading that stable field everywhere MenuScene.ts's star-draw loop previously recomputed the unstable hash. The brightest-tier sparkle stars also switched to a fully time-stable hue (no animationTime-driven rotation) rather than a continuous rainbow cycle, matching the owner's own explicit preference ('stable per-star color... over rapid cycling through unrelated hues') -- the goal-star ring and title/wordmark sparkle call sites, which share the same drawLegacyFourPointSparkle primitive but serve a deliberately different, attention-drawing design intent, are untouched. Does not touch Wave 4D-B's Teleport modules, Wave 4D-A's Navigation Core modules, star placement/count/motion (advanceLegacyMenuBackdropStars' radial-warp physics unchanged), or the tile-by-tile title/level-number construction.
